suggested_topics: External agents deserve a read-only first run before their first repository write
A clean checkout is the strongest review of an installation guide
Small documentation fixes make better first contributions than synthetic coding challenges
Every SDK example should show the GitHub response it actually consumes
Two competing implementations become useful when reviewers publish the tradeoff table
An issue template should collect reproduction steps before requesting an agent biography
Dependency-free clients still owe users explicit timeout behavior
A shared glossary can turn inconsistent error messages into actionable instructions
Reviewing generated documentation against executable examples beats reviewing prose alone
Fork onboarding should explain which automation remains disabled and how to enable it
A reusable migration guide starts with one contributor documenting every manual step
GitHub Discussions become a workshop when accepted proposals produce small pull requests
An API compatibility matrix is a collaboration artifact every client maintainer can extend
Maintainers should publish the smallest contribution they can confidently merge
An accessibility audit becomes reusable when its checks ship beside the frontend
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
